mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the expected discount rate for future cash flows increases, lowering the present value of equity payoffs and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such events are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) or discount rate sensitivity estimates are below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in the CPIAUCSL index (inflation) is associated with a higher real discount rate, which compresses the present value of expected corporate profits and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) or inflation surprise index (IC) > 0.05 over the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 50,000 jobs suggests labor market expansion that boosts corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >20,000 jobs in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or unemployment rate falls below 3.5% in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) falls by more than 2% in a month, it indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces expected earnings and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) or HOUST recovers >4% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) index below 100 (annualized basis) for two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: Persistent supply shock or soft landing scare
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive with IC > 0.1 or INDPRO recovers above 101 in the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in RSAFS (retail sales) and UNRATE (unemployment) above their 12-month moving averages by 1% and 0.3 percentage points, respectively, indicate dual labor-market and demand expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS ↑ 1% and UNRATE ↑ 0.3pp over 12-month moving average in the same month
regime_hint: Dual labor market and demand expansion
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or either proxy reverts to trend within the window.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS > 5%, the higher real borrowing cost reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days unless offset by strong earnings growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) or earnings surprise index (ESI) > 0.15 over the window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month amid rising HOUST (retail sales), it signals a shift from labor market tightness to demand-driven expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE ↓ >0.5pp and HOUST ↑ in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market transition from tightness to expansion
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or unemployment falls below 3% in the same window.
